parsed.title: Intersective sets contain a difference of two primes
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the set of primes, and let $\mathbb{P}-\mathbb{P}=\{p-q:p,q\in\mathbb{P}\}$. A set $R\subset\mathbb{N}$ is **intersective** if it meets $S-S$ for every subset $S\subset\mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density.

**Intersective prime-difference conjecture.** For every intersective set $R$,

$$
R\cap(\mathbb{P}-\mathbb{P})\neq\varnothing.
$$

The paper explains that this would follow for every intersective set from the stronger expected inclusion $\mathbb{P}-\mathbb{P}\supset 2\mathbb{Z}$, but seeks the stated conclusion unconditionally. Its status is open.
parsed.source_name: Pierre-Yves Bienvenu, John T. Griesmer, Anh N. Le and Thái Hoàng Lê, “Intersective sets for sparse sets of integers”, arXiv:2401.07758 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07758

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

parsed.title: Band induction conjecture for tripod Nim bands
parsed.statement:
Let $C_c(a,b)$ denote the quantity associated with the tripod Nim array parameterized by $c$, and say that the numbers from $0$ through $m$ **form a band** when the corresponding band condition holds. Fix $c \in \mathbb{N}$. **Band induction conjecture.** If there exist $N,k$ such that, for all $a,b>N$, 
$$
|a-b| \leq 4k-1 \iff C_c(a,b) \leq 8k-2,
$$
 then there exists $N'$ such that, for all $a,b>N'$, 
$$
|a-b| \leq 4k+3 \iff C_c(a,b) \leq 8k+6.
$$
 This conjecture asserts an inductive extension of a band from radius $4k$ to radius $4k+4$; the surrounding discussion relates it to the stability of periodic orbits of $D(8,4n)$, but no proof or resolution is supplied here.
parsed.source_name: Aidan Hennessey, “Tree and Tripod Nim”, arXiv:2401.07943 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.07943

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

parsed.title: Congruence conjecture for initial RGB-tilings
parsed.statement:
Let $EP$ be an exceptional polyhedron and let $E(EP)$ denote its edge set. An **initial RGB-tiling** is an RGB-tiling on the graph obtained by deleting one edge from $EP$.

**Congruence conjecture.** For every fixed $e\in E(EP)$, all possible initial RGB-tilings on $EP-\{e\}$ are congruent to each other.

This conjecture concerns the uniqueness, up to congruence, of the initial RGB-tilings used in the paper's approach to the Four Color Theorem. The supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or refuted.
parsed.source_name: Shu-Chung Liu, “A sequel to the adventure of RGB-tilings to explore the Four Color Theorem”, arXiv:2401.12222 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12222

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

parsed.title: Duality conjecture for recovery balanced codes
parsed.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a linear code over a finite field, and let $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ denote its dual code. A code is **recovery balanced** when its random access expectation is equal to its dimension $k$.

**Duality conjecture.** A code $\mathcal{C}$ is recovery balanced if and only if its dual code $\mathcal{C}^\perp$ is recovery balanced.

The conjecture would extend the result proved for codes whose permutation automorphism group is transitive. It is supported by the fact that MDS, Hamming, and simplex codes are recovery balanced over every finite field, but the general closure of recovery balancedness under duality remains open.
parsed.source_name: Anina Gruica, Daniella Bar-Lev, Alberto Ravagnani and Eitan Yaakobi, “A Combinatorial Perspective on Random Access Efficiency for DNA Storage”, arXiv:2401.15722 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.15722

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

parsed.title: Paired coalition number conjecture for complete binary trees
parsed.statement:
Let $T(h)$ denote a complete binary tree with height $h$, and let $PC(T(h))$ denote its paired coalition number.

**Complete binary tree conjecture.**

$$
PC(T(h))=\begin{cases}5 & \text{if } h=2,\\3 & \text{if } h \text{ is odd},\\0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture gives the proposed paired coalition number for every complete binary tree. The preceding argument establishes the value for $h=4$; the general assertion remains unresolved in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Mohammad Reza Samadzadeh, Doost Ali Mojdeh and Reza Nadimi, “Paired coalition in graphs”, arXiv:2402.10842 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

parsed.title: The forbidden biclique and path conjecture for tree-independence number
parsed.statement: For positive integers $d$ and $s$, a graph is **$\{K_{d,d},P_s\}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{d,d}$ or the $s$-vertex path $P_s$. **The biclique-and-path conjecture.** For any two positive integers $d$ and $s$, the class of $\{K_{d,d},P_s\}$-free graphs has bounded tree-independence number. This is a special case of the finite-forbidden-subgraph conjecture. The case with $P_4$ is discussed as known, while the full statement for arbitrary $d$ and $s$ remains open.
parsed.source_name: Clément Dallard, Matjaž Krnc, O-joung Kwon, Martin Milanič, Andrea Munaro, Kenny Štorgel and Sebastian Wiederrecht, “Treewidth versus clique number. IV. Tree-independence number of graphs excluding an induced star”, arXiv:2402.11222 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11222

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “While the conjecture is still open, the following partial results are known.”

parsed.title: Snevily's conjecture on L-intersecting families of subsets
parsed.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. For a set of nonnegative integers $\mathcal{L}=\{l_1,l_2,\dots,l_s\}$, a family $\mathcal{A}=\{A_1,A_2,\dots,A_m\}$ of subsets of $[n]$ is **$\mathcal{L}$-intersecting** when $|A_i\cap A_j|\in\mathcal{L}$ for every pair of distinct members. Let $K=\{k_1,k_2,\dots,k_r\}$ be a set of positive integers, and suppose that $|A_i|\in K$ for every $1\leq i\leq m$. **Snevily's conjecture.** If $\max\{l_i\}<\min\{k_j\}$, then

$$
|\mathcal{A}|\leq {{n}\choose{s}}.
$$

The conjecture would considerably improve several earlier bounds for $\mathcal{L}$-intersecting families and remains unresolved in the stated generality.
parsed.source_name: Jiuqiang Liu, Guihai Yu, Lihua Feng and Yongjiang Wu, “Snevily's Conjecture about L-intersecting Families on Set Systems and its Analogue on Vector Spaces”, arXiv:2403.04139 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04139

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

parsed.title: Symmetry of the counting function in a unitary polar-space construction
parsed.statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $b\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ satisfy $b^{q+1}=-1$, and let $(s,u,w)\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}^3$ satisfy

$$
s^{q+1}=u^{q+1}+w^{q+1}.
$$

For each $\kappa\in\mathbb{F}_q^*$, let $n(\kappa)$ be the number of values of $\lambda\in\mathbb{F}_{q^2}\cup\{\infty\}$ satisfying

$$
(w\lambda+1)(b+u\lambda)^q-(w\lambda+1)^q(b+u\lambda)=\kappa\left(b^2+1+\lambda^2(s^2-u^2-w^2)\right)^{(q+1)/2}.
$$

**Counting-function symmetry conjecture.** For every $\kappa\in\mathbb{F}_q^*$, one has

$$
n(\kappa)=n(-\kappa).
$$

This conjecture is introduced to support a construction concerning unitary groups acting on totally isotropic $k$-spaces. The source does not report a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
parsed.source_name: John Bamberg, Michael Giudici, Jesse Lansdown and Gordon F. Royle, “Tactical decompositions in finite polar spaces and non-spreading classical group actions”, arXiv:2403.17576 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17576

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

parsed.title: Hibi–Li's f-vector conjecture for order and chain polytopes
parsed.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset with $|P|=d>1$. Write $f_i(Q)$ for the number of $i$-dimensional faces of a polytope $Q$, and let ${\mathcal O}(P)$ and ${\mathcal C}(P)$ denote the order polytope and chain polytope of $P$, respectively. **Hibi–Li's conjecture.** For every $i$ with $1\leq i\leq d-1$, 

$$
f_i({\mathcal O}(P))\leq f_i({\mathcal C}(P)).
$$

Moreover, if equality holds for some $i$ with $1\leq i\leq d-1$, then ${\mathcal O}(P)$ and ${\mathcal C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent. Hibi and Li proposed this as a comparison of the face numbers of order and chain polytopes; the paper's abstract proves the relevant inequality for triangular $2$-faces when $P$ is maximal ranked, but the full conjecture is not resolved here.
parsed.source_name: Aki Mori, “Triangular faces of the order and chain polytope of a maximal ranked poset”, arXiv:2404.00263 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.00263

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

parsed.title: Alon et al.'s additivity conjecture for joins of low-inversion graphs
parsed.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $D_1,\ldots,D_k$ be oriented graphs. The **$k$-join** $[D_1,\ldots,D_k]$ is formed from vertex-disjoint copies of these graphs by adding every edge from $D_i$ to $D_j$ whenever $i<j$. **Alon et al.'s join additivity conjecture.** If $\operatorname{inv}(D_i)\leq 2$ for every $i$, then 
$$
\operatorname{inv}([D_1,\ldots,D_k])=\sum_{i=1}^k\operatorname{inv}(D_i).
$$
 The cited result proves this when at most one factor has inversion number two; the conjecture asserts that this restriction is unnecessary.
parsed.source_name: Natalie Behague, Tom Johnston, Natasha Morrison and Shannon Ogden, “A note on inverting the dijoin of oriented graphs”, arXiv:2404.10663 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10663

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

parsed.title: Generalized stability conjecture for binary scalar products
parsed.statement:
Let ${\mathscr{A}},{\mathscr{B}}\subseteq{\mathbb{R}}^d$ be families of vectors that both linearly span ${\mathbb{R}}^d$. Assume that

$$
\langle a,b\rangle\in\{0,1\}
$$

for every $a\in{\mathscr{A}}$ and $b\in{\mathscr{B}}$. For some $k\in[0,d]$, also assume that

$$
|{\mathscr{A}}|,|{\mathscr{B}}|>2^{k-1}(d-k+2).
$$

**Generalized stability conjecture.** Then

$$
|{\mathscr{A}}|\,|{\mathscr{B}}|\leq(2^{d-k}+k)2^k(d-k+1).
$$

This conjecture is presented as a generalization of the paper's preceding theorems; the supplied text gives no resolution evidence.
parsed.source_name: Andrey Kupavskii and Dmitry Tsarev, “Stability for binary scalar products”, arXiv:2404.17933 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17933

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2024). “This was proved in a recent work by Kupavskii and Weltge.”

parsed.title: The connectivity conjecture for the generating graph of finite groups
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $\bar\Delta(G)$ denote its generating graph, whose vertices represent the elements of $G$ and whose edges join pairs that generate $G$. **Generating-graph connectivity conjecture.** The graph $\bar\Delta(G)$ is connected for every finite group $G$. This conjecture concerns how generating pairs are distributed among the elements of finite groups. Connectivity is known for several classes, including soluble and characteristically simple groups, but the assertion for all finite groups remains open.
parsed.source_name: Andrea Lucchini and Daniele Nemmi, “On the connectivity of the generating and rank graphs of finite groups”, arXiv:2405.16427 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16427

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

parsed.title: Simplicity conjecture for the characteristic polynomial of a randomized subtraction game
parsed.statement:
Let $t$ be the number of allowed moves, and let $d_1,\ldots,d_t$ be the corresponding positive integers, with characteristic polynomial

$$
\chi_S(x)=tx^{d_t}+\sum_{i=1}^{t-1}x^{d_i}+1.
$$

**Simplicity conjecture.** The roots of $\chi_S(x)$ are all simple whenever $d_t\equiv 1\pmod{2}$ and $d_i\equiv 0\pmod{2}$ for all $1\leq i\leq t-1$.

This conjecture concerns the case not covered by the preceding convergence theorem and would permit the authors' argument to proceed under the assumption that all roots are simple. The source gives no proof or resolution of the claim.
parsed.source_name: Nicolas Capitelli and Francisco Somma, “On sequences arising from randomizing subtraction games”, arXiv:2405.19593 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19593

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

parsed.title: Generalized forbidden out-degree conjecture
parsed.statement: Let $G$ be a loopless graph, and let $d(v)$ denote the degree of each vertex $v\in V(G)$. Given a function $F:V(G)\to 2^{\mathbb N}$, an orientation is **$F$-avoiding** if its out-degree $d_D^+(v)$ satisfies $d_D^+(v)\notin F(v)$ for every $v\in V(G)$. **Generalized forbidden out-degree conjecture.** If $|F(v)|<\tfrac{1}{2}d(v)$ for all $v\in V(G)$, then $G$ admits an $F$-avoiding orientation. This generalization is motivated by allowing the degree and forbidden list to vary from vertex to vertex. The source verifies it for some new cases, including 2-degenerate graphs and forbidden sets with specific structure, but the full statement remains open.
parsed.source_name: Owen Henderschedt and Jessica McDonald, “On orientations with forbidden out-degrees”, arXiv:2406.05095 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05095

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

parsed.title: Koszulity conjecture for cohomology rings of graph modular compactifications
parsed.statement: Let $\operatorname{\Gamma}$ be a connected graph, and let $H^{\bullet}(\operatorname{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(\operatorname{\Gamma}))$ denote the cohomology ring of its graph modular compactification. **Koszulity conjecture.** The cohomology ring $H^{\bullet}(\operatorname{\overline{\mathcal{M}}}(\operatorname{\Gamma}))$ is Koszul. Koszulity is known in the cited special cases of chordal graphs, while the claim for arbitrary connected graphs is presented as a suspected generalization and remains open in the supplied text.
parsed.source_name: Anton Khoroshkin and Denis Lyskov, “Hilbert series for contractads and modular compactifications”, arXiv:2406.05909 (2024).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05909

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

parsed.title: The generalized Grassmann–Plücker exchange conjecture for matroid bases
parsed.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be bases of a matroid $\mathbf{M}$ with rank function $r$. For any $X\subseteq A\setminus B$ and $Y\subseteq B\setminus A$ and integer $p$ with $|Y| \le p \le |X|$, there should exist $U \subseteq A\setminus B$ and $V \subseteq B\setminus A$ such that

$$
|U\cap X|=p,\qquad Y\subseteq V,\qquad |U|=|V|\le r((U\cap X)\cup Y),
$$

and $A\setminus U\cup V$ and $B\cup U\setminus V$ are bases. **Generalized Grassmann–Plücker exchange conjecture.** The stated exchange property holds for every matroid. This would provide a common generalization of the paper's equitability-exchange theorem and its main theorem: it recovers the latter when $p=|X|$ and specializes to the former, with additional upper bounds on $|U|$ and $|V|$, when $p=|X|-1\ge |Y|$.
parsed.source_name: Taihei Oki and Tamás Schwarcz, “Generalizing the Multiple Exchange Property for Matroid Bases”, arXiv:2511.16021 (2026).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16021

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

parsed.title: The QUP polar-code functional inequality assumption
parsed.statement:
Let $h:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ be a non-negative function, and let $q>0$ be a constant such that

$$
2h(z)=q\bigl(h(z^2)+h(2z-z^2)\bigr)
$$

for every $z\in[0,1]$.

**QUP polar-code functional inequality.** Then

$$
h(z_1)+h(z_2)\leq q\bigl(h(z_1z_2)+h(z_1+z_2-z_1z_2)\bigr)
$$

for every $z_1,z_2\in[0,1]$.

This assumption is used in the analysis of QUP polar codes. The supplied text does not establish the implication or provide evidence resolving it, so its status remains open.
parsed.source_name: Yuan Li, Zicheng Ye, Huazi Zhang, Jun Wang, Wen Tong, Guiying Yan and Zhiming Ma, “Stitched Polar Codes”, arXiv:2511.19249 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.19249

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

parsed.title: Orbit length conjecture for iterated bridge sums of trees and complete graphs
parsed.statement: Let $G_1=(V_1,E_1),\ldots,G_q=(V_q,E_q)$ be graphs on $n_1,\ldots,n_q$ vertices, respectively, where each $G_i$ is either a complete graph or a tree. Form $G$ by bridge summing $G_1$ with $G_2$, $G_2$ with $G_3$, and so on, at arbitrary vertices. Let $V'=V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_q$ and let $N=|V'|$. **Iterated bridge-sum orbit-length conjecture.** For all such $G$, the orbit length of toric promotion on $G$ is $N(N-1)$. This is known when all the summands are trees, but remains open for arbitrary mixtures of trees and complete graphs.
parsed.source_name: Kerry Seekamp, “Orbits of toric promotion on bridge sums”, arXiv:2512.00692 (2025).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00692

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

parsed.title: Fixed-order MLDE conjecture for generalized Schur partition functions
parsed.statement:
Let a 4d ${\cal N}=2$ superconformal field theory have rank $r$, 4d central charge $c_{\rm 4d}$, and associated BPS monodromy matrix $M$. For each $k$, define

$$
{\cal I}_k(q) \coloneq q^{\frac12 c(k)}(q;q)_\infty^{2r}\,{\rm Tr}\, M^k.
$$

Here

$$
c(k)=-k\,c_{\rm 4d}+\frac{r\,(k+1)}{6}.
$$

**Fixed-order MLDE conjecture.** For any given 4d ${\cal N}=2$ superconformal field theory, ${\cal I}_k(q)$ solves a modular linear differential equation of fixed order and Wronskian index, for all $k$. This conjecture proposes a uniform modular-differential-equation structure for traces of powers of BPS monodromy matrices; the source motivates it by the observed generalized Schur partition functions and their fixed-order and fixed-Wronskian-index MLDEs, but gives no general proof.
parsed.source_name: A. Ramesh Chandra, Sunil Mukhi and Palash Singh, “Generalised 4d Partition Functions and Modular Differential Equations”, arXiv:2512.02107 (2026).
parsed.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02107

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

parsed.title: Friedgut–Kahn–Kalai–Keller antipodal correlation conjecture
parsed.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be increasing Boolean functions. A Boolean function $g$ is **antipodal** if

$$
g(x)=1-g(1-x)
$$

for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, where $1-x$ is the coordinatewise complement. For a Boolean function $f$, define

$$
\operatorname{Inf}_i[f]=\mathbb{P}[f(x)\neq f(x\oplus e_i)].
$$

**Friedgut–Kahn–Kalai–Keller antipodal correlation conjecture.** For every increasing $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, if $g$ is antipodal, then

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(f,g)\geq \frac14\min_{i\in[n]}\operatorname{Inf}_i[f].
$$

This is presented as an equivalent correlation formulation of Chvátal's conjecture. The supplied text does not state a resolution of either formulation.
parsed.source_name: Fan Chang, “A spectral correlation inequality for increasing Boolean functions”, arXiv:2606.08958 (2026).
parsed.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2025–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2510.22307](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22307).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08958

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
